name: moonbit_gmachine
description: MoonBit G-machine fixture exercising parsing, compilation, lazy graph reduction, algebraic data constructors, recursion, and syntax-error trapping.

exports.name: bad_syntax_traps
exports.description: Harness export that calls the parser on an intentionally malformed Core program and expects the implementation to trap.

exports.name: list_case_matches
exports.description: Harness export that builds a Cons/Nil list and evaluates length through the G-machine runtime.

exports.name: factorial_matches
exports.description: Harness export that evaluates factorial 7 through the sample program definitions.

exports.name: fibs_take_20_matches
exports.description: Harness export that evaluates the first twenty Fibonacci numbers from the documented lazy list program.

tests.description: drive the G-machine compiler and evaluator through numeric, list, recursion, lazy-list, and error paths
tests.notes: The G-machine produces MoonBit strings representing reduced Core values. Each harness export constructs a readable Core-language program, calls the real run() pipeline, and returns 1 only when the full rendered output matches the expected result.

steps.description: evaluate factorial through recursive function calls
steps.notes: Runs '(defn main[] (factorial 7))' with the documented fixture_programs definitions and expects the rendered result '5040'.

steps.description: evaluate list construction and case analysis
steps.notes: Builds '(Cons 10 (Cons 20 (Cons 30 Nil)))', invokes the documented length function, and expects '3'.

steps.description: evaluate a lazy infinite Fibonacci list prefix
steps.notes: Runs '(take 20 fibs)' so the fixture exercises lazy list construction, recursion, arithmetic, and enough graph reduction to produce twenty values.
Passes a missing-parenthesis program into run(). The expected trap verifies that the parser/error path is reached instead of only testing successful reductions.

source.description: Apache-2.0 MoonBit documentation G-machine implementation compiled with a local export harness for corpus tests.

notes: The fixture uses the part3 G-machine from the MoonBit docs. The local harness adds no replacement algorithm; it feeds readable Core-language source strings into the real parser, compiler, and evaluator.
